record.original_question: What is the complexity of the first-order theory of finite trees over finitely many symbols, and is that theory in PSPACE? What is the corresponding complexity for infinite trees?

evidence.quote: What is the complexity of the first-order theory of trees?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a finite signature Σ consisting of finitely many function symbols, each with a specified arity (constants are symbols of arity 0). Let T_fin(Σ) denote the set of finite ground terms built from Σ (the Herbrand universe of finite trees), and let T_inf(Σ) denote the set of finite-or-infinite ground terms (the set of all, possibly infinite, trees labelled by Σ respecting arities). Consider the first-order language with equality whose only non-logical symbols are the function symbols of Σ; interpret these symbols in T_fin(Σ) (resp. T_inf(Σ)) as the natural term-constructor operations.

(a) Determine the exact computational complexity of the first-order theory of (T_fin(Σ), Σ): the set of first-order sentences in this language that are true in T_fin(Σ). In particular, decide whether this theory belongs to PSPACE.

(b) Determine the exact computational complexity of the first-order theory of (T_inf(Σ), Σ), the analogous theory over infinite trees.
artifact.status_search_result: Both theories are known to be decidable (Mal'cev; Maher for infinite/rational trees; Comon and others), and the full first-order theory of finite trees is known to have non-elementary complexity (so it is not in PSPACE), with similar non-elementary lower bounds for the infinite-tree case. Tight complexity characterizations within the non-elementary hierarchy are not fully settled in the literature surveyed, so the precise complexity question is only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: The First-Order Theory of Ordering Constraints over Feature Trees
status_evidence.snippet: The full first-order theory of FT is decidable and has non-elementary complexity.
status_evidence.claim: The first-order theory of finite trees (equality constraints) is decidable but non-elementary, so it is not in PSPACE.

status_evidence.title: Ordering constraints over feature trees (Springer)
status_evidence.snippet: The first-order theory of FT is well-known to be decidable.
status_evidence.claim: Decidability of the first-order theory of finite trees is classical.
